newsitem.title: JAPAN: Relaxed check-up rules to benefit Japan refiners.
newsitem.headline: Relaxed check-up rules to benefit Japan refiners.

text.p: The recent relaxation of refinery maintenance rules in Japan is expected to enable oil firms to cut costs through shorter closure times and a lighter workload for check-ups, refinery sources said on Friday.
"Thanks to the new measures, we can probably keep our plants running 10 more days a year," a refinery official said.

The Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) this month started allowing oil firms to run their plants for up to four years without major maintenance closures, compared with the previous upper limit of two years.
"Based on the results of the our research, we came to a conclusion refineries can be run safely for three to four years without major maintenance checks," a MITI official said.
Some refinery facilities, including boilers and other pressurised vessels, must be inspected every two years, meaning that refiners cannot double the period of continuous operation.
Refiners, however, are able to reduce closure time for maintenance checks from the average 60 days to about 40 days.
The additional 20 working days in two years can roughly be translated into a three percent increase in operating rates, they said.
Operating rates at Japanese refineries traditionally average about 80 percent.
With deregulation, oil firms are anxious for different ministries with jurisdiction to harmonise their regulations.
However, the Labour Ministry, which has control over boilers and other pressurised vessels, said it was not likely to loosen its rules in the near future.
"We are aware of clear and loud voices from the (oil) industry calling for further deregulation," a Labour Ministry official said.
"But we put our priority on safety in the workplace, and I believe it is difficult at present to relax the two-year rule without infringing on that principle," he said.
